_README: Calibration cases for the audio-listening tooling: pairs where a HUMAN's
verdict is on record, so the metrics can be checked against something
Audio is NOT committed. Each case records how to REGENERATE its artifacts
(a git commit to build at, plus the builder invocation), following this
project's existing pattern of regenerating fixtures rather than storing
always, and checks the measured claims only when the artifacts are present.
To add a case: append to `cases`. No new test code is needed.

cases.human_verdict: something with the perc or drums
cases.verdict_source: docs/guides/AUDIO_TIGHTNESS_GUIDE.md (the case that motivated sidm2/audio_tightness.py); docs/players/BLACKBIRD.md B13 entry

bad.commit_subject: Blackbird Stage B12+B13: instrument-select restart timing + gate-off/note translator fix
bad.note: The build the human listened to. Its 'drums sound off' cause was later root-caused and fixed by ef3263b (B25) and 12c7da5 (E3e).

repeatability_floor_pct.description: Original vs a re-render of ITSELF at perturbed power-on delays. The metric's own noise band on this material -- nothing at or above it is evidence.

feature_separation.description: |delta(orig,bad)| - |delta(orig,good)| per feature. POSITIVE means the known-bad build deviates from the original more than the known-good one does, i.e. the feature carries signal about the defect. NEGATIVE means it points the wrong way. Measured 2026-08-09 on the same 60 s sidplayfp delay=0 renders as onset_match_pct.

windowed.description: Improvement #4 (worst_window) run against this case, 5 s windows. Originally DEGENERATE as shipped: silence_frac's confound (a driver render does not reproduce the original's startup silence) is one-directional -- delta = driver - orig is negative in nearly every window regardless of build quality -- and the flat-baseline scoring branch outranges the sigma branch, so silence won outright and flagged both builds identically. FIXED 2026-08-09 by clipping that one direction (_only_more_silent in sidm2/audio_listen.py) rather than dropping the metric outright, so a driver that genuinely goes silent mid-song (the opposite direction) still gets caught.

after_fix.note: Re-measured live against the actual B13 (commit d946701, throwaway worktree) and HEAD builds after the fix, not synthesized. silence_frac's score is now 0.0 for both builds -- fully defanged, not merely excluded -- while RMS/centroid/rolloff/flatness rank normally. The bad build's worst anomaly is mid-song brightness at 15.0s; the good build's is a startup transient. Numbers are close to, but not bit-identical with, the pre-fix 'excluding_silence_frac' figures this replaces (145.956/2.5 -> 150.049/2.576, 5.013/2.75 -> 4.352/2.216) -- both are live sidplayfp renders and small render-to-render drift is expected, not a regression.

chroma.description: Improvement #5 run against this case. B13 was a percussive/rhythmic defect, so chroma SHOULD stay quiet -- confirming a metric correctly reports nothing is as useful as watching one fire.
chroma.note: Both builds shift equally and slightly away from C; the separation is ~0. No pitch defect to find, and none reported.

findings.summary: The metric ranks the known-bad build below the known-good one (56.9 < 64.7), so it has ORDINAL sensitivity. It has no usable ABSOLUTE calibration: a 99.8%-register-exact build with 162/162 note-ons still scores 64.7%, more than 20 points below the 85-91% original-vs-itself floor. Any threshold that flags the known-bad build also flags the known-good one. Further, the 7.8-point gap between builds is comparable to the floor's own 5.9-point spread, so a single A/B run cannot separate them confidently.
findings.feature_summary: A-weighting (improvement #2) is the clear win: separation 0.294 (raw dBFS) -> 1.585 (dBA), 5.4x better, and interpretable -- the bad build sits 2.07 dBA from the original where the good build sits 0.48 dBA away. Mel spacing (improvement #1) moves 2 of 3 metrics the right way (centroid -18.613 -> -17.408, flatness 0.019 -> 0.022) and worsens rolloff (-75.441 -> -77.106), but every margin is small; ONE tune cannot establish whether that is a real gain or noise, so read it as unproven here rather than as either a win or a failure. Mel is separately proven correct in isolation -- it resolves a 100/200 Hz octave that linear spacing collapses to -0.0 Hz. Centroid and rolloff show NEGATIVE separation, which is a CONFOUND rather than anti-information: the good build carries more content (32 instruments vs 31, 48 bundles vs 47, 26.9 KB vs 20.8 KB), so more of the song plays and the whole-file spectral average shifts. A whole-file mean cannot separate 'wrong' from 'more complete' -- that is what improvement #4's windowed analysis exists to sidestep.
findings.does_not_address_onset_deficit: Neither #1 nor #2 changes the 20-point onset deficit, and never could: both alter only the feature summary, leaving detect_onsets() on the unchanged linear path by design. onset_match_pct is identical before and after.

cases.human_verdict: sounds really good, [but] there is something not right with the drums... might be filters
cases.verdict_source: docs/players/BLACKBIRD.md, 'B25 SHIPPED' section (2026-07-24) -- recorded AFTER B25 shipped, i.e. the complaint that PERSISTED despite a register-accuracy improvement (97.1%->97.5%). The root cause (filter was actually the strongest category at 99.9%) was found by E3e, not by filter work.
cases.note: SECOND case, same tune as blackbird-glyptodont-b13 but a DIFFERENT commit range isolating a DIFFERENT fix -- chosen deliberately to test whether the metrics' findings (ordinal-only sensitivity, A-weighting as best feature, centroid/rolloff as a completeness confound) replicate on an independent defect, not just restate the first case. Unlike B13 (which spans ~25 commits of compounding fixes), this pair isolates almost exactly the E3b/E3c(c)/E3e fix chain: 'bad' is the commit where the human's complaint was recorded as still-unresolved, 'good' is the commit the docs credit with resolving it.

bad.commit_subject: Blackbird Stage B25: model prepare2's pre-restart SR/gate blip via an fx-command sentinel -- fixes the real "drums sound off" cause, every corpus file improves or is unchanged
bad.note: The state the 'still not right with the drums' complaint was recorded against, despite B25 having just improved the register score.

good.commit_subject: E3e: prepare2 blips from TWO call sites -- the "implicit repeat-instrument" hid 44.8% of all hard restarts
good.note: docs/players/BLACKBIRD.md: 'This is the answer to the user's original "the drums are still not tight"'.

repeatability_floor_pct.description: Original vs a re-render of ITSELF at perturbed power-on delays, measured independently for this case (own script, not reused from the B13 case -- a different render session, different floor).

feature_separation.description: |delta(orig,bad)| - |delta(orig,good)| per feature, same 60 s sidplayfp delay=0 renders as onset_match_pct.

windowed.description: worst_window(), 5 s windows, run after the silence_frac fix (this case was measured entirely post-fix, so there is no 'before_fix' entry to record).

result.note: Same shape as the B13 case despite being a totally different defect/fix: bad's worst window is mid-song centroid at 15.0s (window index 3, matching B13's), good's is a startup RMS transient at 0.0s (window index 0, also matching B13's) -- independent evidence the fix generalizes rather than an artifact of one tune's specific rendering.

chroma.description: The drums/envelope-retrigger defect this case tests has no pitch component, so chroma should again stay quiet.
chroma.note: Both builds shift equally and slightly away from C, same as the B13 case; separation is again ~0. Confirms chroma correctly reports nothing for a second, unrelated non-pitch defect.

findings.summary: Replicates the B13 case's shape on an independent defect: the metric ranks bad below good (56.8 < 65.2), ORDINAL sensitivity again holds, but both builds still score well below their own 84.3-99.8% repeatability floor -- no usable absolute gate here either. Notably, the human's complaint PERSISTED across a register-accuracy improvement (97.1%->97.5%, B25) and was resolved only by a later, different fix (E3e) that moved the register score further (->99.7%) -- a real-world instance of the project's own registers-vs-audio gap, not merely a hypothetical one.
findings.feature_summary: A-weighting is again the clear win here (separation 0.542 -> 1.634, 3.0x), replicating B13's finding independently. Mel spacing again improves 2 of 3 metrics (centroid -15.670 -> -14.527, flatness 0.019 -> 0.021) and again worsens rolloff (-64.579 -> -64.851) -- the exact same 2-of-3 pattern as B13, from an unrelated defect. Centroid and rolloff are again NEGATIVE (a CONFOUND, not anti-information): the good (E3e) build recovers far more of the missing hard-restart note-ons than the bad (B25) build does, so more content plays and the whole-file spectral average shifts, exactly as in B13.
replicates_b13_findings: windowed worst-window window indices (3 for bad, 0 for good)
